title: Richard Dawkins ·《为什么宇宙显得如此奇怪》— 大脑生在「中间世界」，可我们偏偏懂了量子力学
title_en: Richard Dawkins · "Why the universe seems so strange" — our brains were built for Middle World, and yet we cracked quantum mechanics

questions.question: 按 Dawkins「中间世界」的论证，石头几乎全是空的，却摸起来坚硬。这说明了什么？
options: 原子之间的空隙小到肉眼无法分辨，所以我们才误以为石头是实心的
「坚固」是在中等尺度上导航时有用的概念，因为手和石头确实穿不过彼此
「坚硬」只是文化习得的词语，不同语言对它的划分方式并不相同
我们的触觉其实在系统性地欺骗我们，石头远没有我们感到的那么坚硬结实
questions.explanation: Dawkins 说石头摸起来坚硬，恰恰因为石头和手确实穿不过彼此；「坚固」是在中间世界里导航的有用模型，不是错觉。他用维特根斯坦的段子说明的也是这点：眼睛没被骗，「显而易见」只是特定尺度上的显而易见。
questions.question_en: In Dawkins's 'Middle World' argument, rock is almost entirely empty space yet feels hard. What does that show?
options_en: The gaps between atoms are too small to see, so we wrongly assume rock is solid
'Solid' is a useful concept for navigating at medium scale, because hands and rocks really can't pass through each other
'Hard' is a culturally learned word that different languages divide up differently
Our sense of touch systematically deceives us; rock isn't as hard as it feels
questions.explanation_en: Dawkins says rock feels hard precisely because rock and hand can't pass through each other; solidity is a useful model for getting around Middle World, not an illusion. His Wittgenstein anecdote makes the same point: your eyes aren't fooled; 'obvious' is only obvious at a particular scale.

questions.question: 文章援引后来的研究，认为 Dawkins 把直觉的边界画错了位置。真正的分界线在哪里？
options: 在原子尺度和日常尺度之间，正如「中间世界」这个概念所划定的那样
在「感知与动作」和「讲道理、显式推理」之间，而不在尺度大小
在接近光速的高速世界和日常低速世界之间，相对论才是门槛
在受过系统物理训练的人和从没学过物理的人之间
questions.explanation: 1980 年的研究显示，过半大学生连中间世界里的运动轨迹都画错；2013 年的研究又显示，人在看和动的时候是相当准的「直觉物理引擎」。所以演化给的是好用的感知—动作模拟器，不是好用的显式物理理论，哪怕在中间世界里也一样。上过物理课的学生同样画错，训练也不是分界线。
questions.question_en: Citing later research, the article says Dawkins drew the boundary of intuition in the wrong place. Where does it really lie?
options_en: Between the atomic scale and the everyday scale, just as 'Middle World' suggests
Between perception-and-action and explicit reasoning, not between scales
Between near-light-speed worlds and everyday low speeds, where relativity is the threshold
Between people trained in physics and people who never studied it
questions.explanation_en: A 1980 study found most college students misdraw trajectories even in everyday settings, while 2013 work showed people are accurate 'intuitive physics engines' when seeing and acting. Evolution gave us a good perception-action simulator, not a good explicit theory of physics, even in Middle World. Students who had taken physics erred too, so training isn't the line.

questions.question: 对「宇宙可能超出人类能理解的范围」这个悲观推论，文章认为最直接的反例是什么？
options: 蝙蝠、水黾等动物能感知人类感知不到的世界，说明感知可扩展
人类已经掌握了量子力学，只不过是靠数学而不是靠直觉拿下的
量子理论的预测精度高得惊人，这证明我们已经从直觉上真正理解了它
从小玩量子和相对论游戏的孩子，已经被证明养出了相应的直觉
questions.explanation: 文章总结说：科学反直觉是真的，演化塑造直觉也是真的，但推不出人类理解有一道生物学上限——量子力学本身就是反例，只是用数学拿下的。游戏养直觉至今没有研究证明，一篇相关量子游戏论文还被撤稿；预测精确也不等于直觉上懂了。
questions.question_en: Against the pessimistic idea that the universe may lie beyond human understanding, what does the article treat as the most direct counterexample?
options_en: Bats and water striders sense worlds humans can't, showing perception can be extended
Humans have already mastered quantum mechanics, just through mathematics rather than intuition
Quantum theory's astonishing predictive accuracy shows we already grasp it intuitively
Children raised on quantum and relativity games have been shown to develop matching intuitions
questions.explanation_en: The article concludes that science is counterintuitive and evolution shaped intuition, but neither implies a biological ceiling on understanding: quantum mechanics itself is the counterexample, won through math. No study shows games build intuition, and one quantum-game paper was retracted; accurate predictions don't mean intuitive understanding either.
